newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Telekom listing fails to ignite Eurobourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Telekom listing fails to ignite Eurobourses.

text.p: Investors enthusiastically welcomed Europe's biggest share flotation on Monday, paying a healthy premium for Deutsche Telekom shares they failed to secure in the oversubscribed initial offer.
The shares first changed hands in the official market at 33.20 marks, well up on the 28.50 marks the issue was priced at on Sunday.

But with the 20 billion mark ($13.28 billion) flotation of Europe's biggest telecommunications company oversubscribed at least five times over, traders said they expected plenty of demand from investors.

Despite the enthusiasm, however, Germany's 30-share DAX share index traded well down throughout the morning. Paris also fell, although it recovered from its lows and London managed to eke out only a small gain after trading in the minus column for much of the morning.
A shout of "33.20" from a Frankfurt bourse official opened trade in the long-awaited Telekom listing, more than 100 dealers waving their order books at the official brokers handing the issue.
"You hardly ever see the floor trade this busy," commented a bourse spokesman.
More than 26 million shares were bought and sold in the first 20 minutes of trading in Telekom and the price edged up to 33.90 by 1300 GMT.

On foreign exchange markets the dollar was steady against the mark but trading close to its peak for the day against the yen following the first increase in Japan's trade surplus with the United States in 20 months.

Japan's October trade surplus with the U.S. rose 31.3 percent as Japanese car makers took advantage of the weak yen to export more vehicles. But Japan's overall trade surplus fell 12.9 percent in October from a year earlier.
"The headline data was disappointing, but the bilateral surplus positive," said Paul Meggyesi, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
By 1230 GMT the dollar was quoted at 111.48 yen and 1.5068 marks, compared with 111.12 yen and 1.5076 marks in late European trade on Friday.
Sterling was also firmly in the limelight after data showed Britain's October net public sector debt repayment was well above forecasts.
"It's an excellent set of data and clear evidence that the recovery in activity is coming through in tax receipts," said Adam Cole, UK economist at HSBC James Capel.
By 1230 GMT sterling was at 1.6673 dollars against 1.6646 in late Europe on Friday.
London's share market opened firm but swiftly slipped in early trade before inching back above Friday's close by lunchtime.
Traders said the FTSE 100 index was weighed down by lower index futures as continuing worries about British interest rates and the strength of sterling chipped away at sentiment.
"The market lacks follow-through, and I think that really shouldn't be any surprise with retail sales figures on Wednesday and the budget next week," said one dealer.

Shares in British Gas were one focus after press reports said that Anglo-Dutch Shell had approached British Gas with plans for a 40 billion pound ($66.7 billion) merger. The plans, the papers said, went "cold because British Gas had got cold feet." Both firms declined to comment.
French shares cut their losses by midsession after the blue-chip CAC-40 index hit a low of 2,224.17, a level which halted the profit-taking that had pulled shares back from Friday's highs.
Traders said the market would remain in a narrow range, at least until the opening on Wall Street, as it looked for fresh reasons to resume last week's rally.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.48 yen and 1.5068 marks, compared with 111.12 yen and 1.5076 marks in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 1.6 points at 3,959.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 5.18 points at 2,235.15.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 19.17 points at 2,776.63.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $379.70 against $379.25 on Friday afternoon and $379.85 in the morning. Silver firmed seven points to $4.92. ($1=.5994 Pound)
